narrative.overview:
The workspace is the same printed instrument sheet as the front page, set down as a working tool. A light grey ground holds white panels framed in 1px black; corners are square; nothing casts a shadow. The interface speaks in narrow Martian Mono, the page title alone in uppercase Anton, and everything a person reads at length (document passages, answers, quoted excerpts) in Source Serif 4.

Layouts stay familiar and calm: a fixed rail, a capped content column, hairline-ruled rows. Signal red is reserved for the few things that matter at any moment: the primary action under the pointer, the current selection, progress and live work, and keyboard focus. Where something is merely current (the active nav item, the selected document, the active tab), it is a solid ink bar, not a colour. Dark mode is the same sheet inverted: near-black ground, charcoal panels, off-white ink, a brighter red.
keyCharacteristics: Instrument grey ground, white panels, near-black ink, one signal red.
1px strokes everywhere; square corners; no block shadows.
Martian Mono (width 87.5) for the interface, Anton for the page title only, Source Serif 4 for reading.
The current place is a solid ink bar; red marks primary, selected, live, and focus.
Former pastel state fills are neutral greys; the only tint is pale red.
Dark mode is the same system inverted, not a second palette.

rules.name: The Red Means Now Rule
rules.body: Red marks only what is primary, selected, live, focused, or failing. It is never a fill for a notice, banner, or reading panel; a notice is a framed white panel with ink text.

rules.name: The Ink Bar Rule
rules.body: The current place (active nav item, selected document pill, active tab) is a solid ink bar with paper-coloured text. Never a pastel, never a red fill.

rules.name: The Honest Surface Rule
rules.body: Sample files are marked as samples; items added by the user are labeled local; planned AI and server capabilities are described as unavailable.

rules.name: The Three Roles Rule
rules.body: Martian Mono for the interface, Anton for the page title only, Source Serif 4 for reading text only. No fourth family; Anton never appears below the h1, and the serif never sets a control.

rules.name: The Line-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Lift is drawn, never cast. Use a frame, a hairline, or inversion; never a block shadow, blur, or glow.

dos: Do keep red for primary, selected, live, focus, and failure, and the ink bar for the current place.
Do draw every edge as a 1px stroke and keep corners square.
Do set reading text (document chunks, answers, excerpts) in Source Serif 4 and everything else in Martian Mono at width 87.5.
Do keep Anton to the page h1.
Do mark all sample data and prototype-only behavior, and keep unimplemented AI and server capabilities labeled as planned.
Do provide visible keyboard focus and a reduced-motion path.
donts: Don't use red as a fill for notices, banners, or reading panels.
Don't use block shadows, hard offset shadows, blur, glow, gradients, or rounded corners.
Don't bring back mint, sky, or butter hues, or add a second accent.
Don't lift cards or pills on hover; change the frame instead.
Don't imply a file is uploaded, persisted, parsed, or analyzed when it remains in page memory.
Don't use low-contrast grey for running text.

front-page.overview: The front page presents DocuMind as a machine that checks the visitor's own browser live and shows its work. It reads like a printed instrument sheet: a light grey ground ruled with hairlines, black 1px frames, square corners, huge uppercase Anton, and every other word in a narrow monospace. One signal red marks what the machine is pointing at: labels, the cited line, stamps, and live states. Density is high but ordered. Content sits in framed ledgers and ruled rows rather than floating cards, and depth comes from line work, never from blur or block shadows. Every readout shows real data from the visitor's browser or the product's documented facts.
keyCharacteristics: Light grey ground, white framed panels, near-black ink, one red.
1px black frames and 1px hairline grids; square corners throughout.
Anton for display, Martian Mono at width 87.5 for body, labels, readouts, and buttons.
Numbered section marks in a gutter beside the heading.
Live readouts bound to real browser checks.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Signal red is the only accent on the front page. It marks what the machine points at; it never decorates. No second accent, no pastels, no gradients beyond the flat hairline grid.

rules.name: The Real Readout Rule
rules.body: Every number or status the page displays comes from the visitor's browser (WebGPU, free storage, model cache) or from documented product facts. A readout without a real source does not ship.

rules.name: The Two Faces Rule
rules.body: Anton is reserved for display and headline sizes and the large preview figures. Everything else is Martian Mono at width 87.5; never introduce a third family or a system display face.

rules.name: The Line-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Lift is drawn, never cast. Use a frame, a hairline, an offset second frame, or inversion; never a block shadow, blur, or glow.

dos: Do keep Signal Red (#d3110f) as the only accent, used for section marks, the cited line, stamps, citations, and live states.
Do draw depth with 1px frames, hairlines, the offset second frame, or inversion.
Do bind every readout to a real browser check or a documented product fact, and show an honest unknown when a check cannot resolve.
Do set section numbers /01 to /07 in the gutter beside the heading's first line, topped by a 1px red rule.
Do keep Anton for display and headline sizes and Martian Mono at width 87.5 for everything else.
donts: Don't use block shadows, hard offset shadows, blur, glow, or rounded corners on the front page.
Don't add a second accent color or carry mint, sky, or butter onto the front page.
Don't invent stats, user counts, customer names, or logos.
Don't place section numbers above a heading as an eyebrow or kicker.
